sources.title: Andreas Neubauer and Ronny Ramlau, Lecture Notes: Integral Equations and Boundary Value Problems
sources.locator: Chapter 2, §2.2 (printed pp. 15–16); Chapter 3, §3.3, Method 3.12, equations (3.18)–(3.23), Definitions 3.13–3.14, Lemmas 3.15–3.17, Theorems 3.18–3.19, Corollary 3.20 and Remarks 3.21–3.22 (printed pp. 60–65).
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete author-hosted lecture-notes PDF; the Nyström section and the continuous-kernel compactness argument were inspected in full.
sources.not_read: The complete relevant arguments in Chapter 2 §2.2 and Chapter 3 §3.3 were read. Other chapters are outside this pair and are not cited as proof support.

contents.name: Chapter 2 §2.2: a continuous kernel gives a compact integral operator on C[0,1]
contents.support: The item supplies a complete local equicontinuity and Arzelà–Ascoli proof with the explicit Countable Choice and Dependent Choice hypotheses.

contents.name: Method 3.12 and equations (3.18)–(3.23): Nyström operator, sampled system and reconstruction
contents.support: The local definition fixes the real C([0,1]) convention and the local finite-node lemma proves the solution correspondence in full.

contents.name: Method 3.12: quadrature weights enter the reconstructed Nyström operator
contents.support: The local item specializes the general weight convention to the half-order hat weights and proves each closed form from one-sided antiderivatives.

contents.name: Definition 3.13: collective compactness
contents.support: The local theorem states the unit-ball form and proves eventual inverse stability directly.

contents.name: Definition 3.14: collectively compact convergence
contents.support: The local midpoint lemma proves pointwise norm consistency and collective compactness for the selected rule.

contents.name: Lemma 3.15: the pointwise limit of a collectively compact sequence is compact
contents.support: Used as comparison for the stability framework; compactness of the specific integral operator is proved locally in its own supplier.

contents.name: Lemma 3.16: composition errors (K-K_n)K and (K-K_n)K_n tend to zero
contents.reason: The local collectively compact stability proof uses a lower-bound contradiction and the supplied Fredholm alternative; no composition-norm convergence claim is needed.

contents.name: Lemma 3.17: inverse perturbation estimate for compact operators
contents.reason: The pair proves its own Fredholm stability argument and a separate Neumann norm-perturbation branch; this intermediate theorem is not a dependency.

contents.name: Theorem 3.18: collectively compact approximation and solution error
contents.support: This is the source framework for the local AC-dependent theorem; the carrier gives a complete proof with explicit choice uses.

contents.name: Theorem 3.19: Nyström operators from convergent quadrature are collectively compact and consistent
contents.support: The local proof specializes to composite midpoint weights and does not assume an operator-norm bound.

contents.name: Corollary 3.20: Nyström solvability and solution convergence
contents.support: The local error theorem derives the residual estimate for the fixed smooth solution integrand.

contents.name: Remark 3.21: error depends on the quadrature residual and nonnegative weights control stability
contents.support: The page records the actual-integrand regularity hypothesis and separately proves positive weight stability for product integration.

contents.name: Remark 3.22: an iterative method for solving the Nyström system
contents.reason: No iterative solver or iteration convergence claim is part of this pair.

read_evidence.access_method: The complete PDF was fetched directly, converted with MuPDF for inspection, and the full Chapter 2 §2.2 and Chapter 3 §3.3 argument blocks were read.
read_evidence.extent: Printed pp. 15–16 and 60–65, including Method 3.12 through Remark 3.22. Lemmas 3.16–3.17 and the iterative-method remark were inspected and recorded as out of scope.

sources.title: Habib Ammari, Brian Fitzpatrick, and Sanghyeon Yu, Mathematical and Computational Methods in Photonics: Tutorial Notes
sources.locator: Chapter 1, §§1.3–1.4, Definitions 1.1–1.2 and 1.6, Theorems 1.4–1.12, and Remark 1.13 (printed pp. 10–17).
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete author-hosted tutorial-notes PDF; the operator-approximation and Nyström sections were inspected in full.
sources.not_read: The full relevant reasoning in §§1.3–1.4 was inspected. The rest of the tutorial is not used for this pair.

contents.name: Definitions 1.1–1.2: pointwise and operator-norm convergence
contents.support: The local midpoint lemma proves pointwise norm convergence; the norm perturbation theorem states its stronger hypothesis explicitly.

contents.name: Theorem 1.4 and Theorem 1.5: Neumann inversion and norm perturbation stability
contents.support: The local proof invokes the published Neumann-series supplier and derives the inverse and residual estimates.

contents.name: Definition 1.6: collectively compact operator families
contents.support: The local stability and midpoint arguments state and verify the relevant compact-closure property.

contents.name: Theorem 1.7: convergence property of collectively compact operators
contents.reason: The printed theorem repeats the same expression in both displayed limits; the local proof does not rely on this malformed second assertion.

contents.name: Theorem 1.8: compact-operator Fredholm alternative
contents.support: The local theorem uses the separately published Fredholm alternative, whose Axiom of Choice hypothesis is stated explicitly.

contents.name: Theorem 1.9: approximation through pointwise convergence
contents.support: The local theorem proves eventual invertibility and the residual error estimate directly; the printed theorem statement has a sign typo in its right-hand-side difference, so no source formula is copied.

contents.name: Section 1.4.1 and Theorem 1.10: quadrature Nyström equation and sampled-system equivalence
contents.support: The local finite-node lemma gives a full algebraic proof; the printed theorem has typographical omissions in its displayed equation.

contents.name: Theorem 1.11: pointwise/collective compactness and failure of norm convergence
contents.support: The theorem heading reverses the direction stated in its body; the local constant-kernel counterexample proves the exact operator-norm value independently.

contents.name: Theorem 1.12 and Remark 1.13: Nyström solution convergence and inherited quadrature order
contents.support: The page derives the smooth-solution rate from the supplied midpoint error bound and the local stability theorem, with no reliance on the source proof’s earlier sign typo.

contents.name: §1.4 discussion of singular kernels and method-specific product quadrature
contents.support: This motivates the separate half-order product-integration construction; its weights and error estimates are proved locally.

read_evidence.access_method: The complete PDF was fetched directly, converted with MuPDF, and §§1.3–1.4 were read in full.
read_evidence.extent: Printed pp. 10–17, including all displayed proof steps and the source’s typos in Theorems 1.7, 1.9, 1.10, and the title of 1.11; those issues are recorded above and are not imported as proof claims.

sources.title: Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis I, §5.5 Improper Integrals
sources.locator: §5.5, Definition 5.5.1 and Proposition 5.5.2, the endpoint p-test for 0<p<1; the p=1/2 instance is used.
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete open textbook section in HTML; the improper-Riemann definition and full p-test proof were inspected.
sources.not_read: The complete §5.5 reasoning at the cited definition and proposition was read; unrelated sections and other improper-integral examples are not used.

contents.name: Definition 5.5.1: endpoint improper Riemann integral as a one-sided limit
contents.support: The local scalar lemma defines the two-sided diagonal truncation and proves its limit using the p=1/2 estimate.

contents.name: Proposition 5.5.2: endpoint integrability of y^{-p} for 0<p<1
contents.support: The p=1/2 case motivates the exact integral; the local item evaluates both sides of the diagonal and its operator norm.

contents.name: Endpoint p-test used to establish integrability of the translated half-order singularities
contents.support: The local lemma proves the improper L1 difference exists and then establishes a uniform translation modulus by truncation and continuous smoothing.

contents.name: Endpoint p=1/2 integral used in the exact closed form of the piecewise-linear product weights
contents.support: The item derives the panel primitives and every endpoint/interior hat-weight formula directly; this source supports convergence of the improper endpoint term.

contents.name: Other §5.5 examples and p-test cases
contents.reason: Only the endpoint p=1/2 integrability input is used; other powers and unrelated improper-integral examples do not support claims in this pair.

read_evidence.access_method: The full HTML section was opened and its definition, proposition, and complete proof were inspected.
read_evidence.extent: §5.5 Definition 5.5.1 and Proposition 5.5.2, with the complete endpoint p-test reasoning for p=1/2.
